headline: KSE-100 rebounds 641 points as KP ratification clears NA and Senate, while hot US CPI sends Wall Street and metals sharply lower
mood: Cautiously constructive · KP resolution in sight, global risk-off lingers

snapshot.label: US 10Y / 2Y
snapshot.delta: hot CPI lifts Dec hike odds to ~85%

five_things.chip: KSE-100 Rebounds 641 Points as KP Ratification Clears NA and Senate
five_things.html: The KSE-100 reversed two sessions of selling, climbing 641.07 points (+0.39%) to close at 165,417.51 on Wednesday after swinging between an intraday low of 164,060.34 and a high of 165,629.35. Buying in ENGROH, LUCK, FFC, BAHL and NBP added a combined 381 points to the index, while refinery names led by Pakistan Refinery Limited drew fresh interest; market-wide turnover held firm at roughly 586 million shares worth Rs 20.1 billion, with WTL topping the volume chart at 87 million shares. The catalyst: the National Assembly and Senate both ratified the federal emergency proclamation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Wednesday — PTI lawmakers staged a walkout in protest — clearing the way for today's 11:30am joint sitting to formally ratify Governor's Rule under Article 234, with PPP having ended its boycott to back the resolution. Business Recorder and Daily Times confirm the levels.
five_things.sentiment: relief rally, political resolution in sight

five_things.chip: Hot US CPI Jolts Wall Street, December Fed Hike Odds Surge
five_things.html: US stocks sold off Wednesday after September CPI came in hotter than expected at 3.7% y/y (vs 3.6% forecast) with core CPI at 2.6% y/y (vs 2.5% forecast): the Nasdaq lost 1.88% to 26,692.87, the S&P 500 fell 1.11% to 7,718.94 and the Dow slipped a milder 0.09% to 51,621.48. Fed-funds futures and prediction markets repriced sharply, with December rate-hike odds jumping to roughly 83–89% from ~72% a day earlier, and traders now debating whether the Fed delivers a double hike or a 50bp move before year-end. TheStreet and CNBC confirm the figures.

five_things.chip: Gold, Silver Slammed as Inflation Surprise Revives Rate-Hike Bets
five_things.html: Precious metals took the CPI shock hardest: COMEX gold settled at $4,120.82, down about 1.0%, after briefly trading below $4,100 intraday, while silver cratered 5.9% to $55.70, giving back a chunk of its recent run as the firmer dollar and higher yields pulled speculative longs out. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.19% after an earlier CPI-driven spike, while the 2-year held near 4.82%. Comex Live and Business Standard confirm the settles.

five_things.chip: OPEC+ Holds November Quotas Steady as Hormuz Risk Keeps Oil Elevated
five_things.html: The seven-nation OPEC+ core group — led by Saudi Arabia and Russia — kept November output quotas unchanged at a combined 31.01 million bpd, extending the pause it started in October as conflict-related disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz continue to keep actual output below targeted levels; the group reconvenes on 1 November. Brent held near $105.43 and WTI near $95.17, keeping the energy-import bill elevated for oil-importing economies including Pakistan. World Oil and Trading Economics confirm the levels.

five_things.chip: Tadawul Slides 1.74% in Broad Gulf Risk-Off, Even as Oil Holds Firm
five_things.html: Saudi Arabia's Tadawul All-Share Index fell 179.31 points (−1.74%) to close at 10,138.83, with breadth decisively negative (252 decliners vs just 15 advancers) on turnover of roughly SR3.9 billion (~$1.04bn); the parallel Nomu index dropped 0.90% to 21,832.37. The pullback came despite firm oil prices, underscoring that the region's risk-off impulse — tied to the broader Hormuz/security overhang and the global rates repricing — is currently outweighing the energy tailwind. Arab News confirms the close.

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's tape found its footing: the KSE-100 rebounded 641.07 points (+0.39%) to 165,417.51 after an early dip to 164,060.34, as buying in ENGROH, LUCK, FFC, BAHL, NBP and the refinery counters offset the prior session's losses. The driver was political progress rather than reversal: the National Assembly and Senate both ratified the KP emergency proclamation on Wednesday — PTI staged a walkout in protest — clearing the runway for today's 11:30am joint sitting to formally impose Governor's Rule under Article 234, backed by an 11-member advisory council, after PPP ended its legislative boycott to support the resolution. The macro backdrop stayed supportive: the rupee held effectively flat at 276.95 interbank (+Re0.01), the SBP policy rate remains at 11.5% ahead of its next review on 26 October, September CPI was last confirmed at 10.3% y/y, and the $1.2bn IMF tranche still awaits Executive Board sign-off. Business Recorder and Business Recorder.
matrix.gcc_html: Gulf markets moved the other way: Saudi Arabia's Tadawul All-Share Index fell 1.74% to 10,138.83 on broad-based selling (252 decliners vs 15 advancers, SR3.9bn turnover), with the Nomu parallel market off 0.90% to 21,832.37 — a reminder that regional risk appetite remains fragile even as energy prices hold firm. OPEC+ kept November output quotas unchanged at a combined 31.01 million bpd, extending its pause as Hormuz-linked disruptions keep actual supply below target, with the group's core seven reconvening 1 November; Brent held near $105.43 and WTI near $95.17. The UAE's VAT Executive Regulation amendments (Cabinet Decision No. 149) remain in force, continuing to weigh on SME compliance costs even as the broader non-oil diversification story (Saudi and UAE non-oil PMI both near 55.3 in September) stays intact. Arab News and World Oil.
matrix.global_html: Wall Street absorbed a hawkish inflation surprise: September CPI printed 3.7% y/y (vs 3.6% expected) with core at 2.6% y/y, sending the Nasdaq down 1.88% to 26,692.87, the S&P 500 down 1.11% to 7,718.94 and the Dow off a milder 0.09% to 51,621.48. Treasury yields whipsawed before settling — the 10-year eased to 5.19% and the 2-year held near 4.82% — while December Fed hike odds jumped to roughly 83–89% from ~72% a day earlier, with some desks now debating a 50bp move. The repricing hit precious metals hardest: gold settled at $4,120.82 (−1.0%) and silver slid 5.9% to $55.70. On the fiscal side, Washington remains funded under the continuing resolution through 11 December, pushing the next shutdown risk past the midterms. TheStreet and CNBC.

legislative.policy_html: NA and Senate ratification of the KP emergency proclamation on Wednesday clears the way for today's 11:30am joint sitting to formally impose Governor's Rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Article 234, backed by an 11-member advisory council; PPP ended its boycott to support the resolution while PTI walked out in protest.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: the federal government, security apparatus and PPP, which banks political capital for backing the centre; equities, which rallied 0.39% as the path to resolution firmed. Loses: PTI, sidelined after its walkout, and KP's provincial autonomy, which remains suspended pending today's formal ratification.

legislative.policy_html: OPEC+'s decision to hold November output quotas at 31.01 million bpd continues to anchor Gulf supply discipline, while the UAE's VAT Executive Regulation amendments (Cabinet Decision No. 149) remain in force for compliant corporates and burdened SMEs alike.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Gulf oil producers and energy majors, which keep benefiting from Brent above $105 and disciplined supply; large UAE corporates already compliant with the VAT apportionment rules. Loses: UAE SMEs still absorbing VAT-compliance costs, and broader Gulf risk sentiment, which stayed firmly negative (Tadawul −1.74%, 252 decliners vs 15 advancers) even with oil holding firm.

legislative.policy_html: A hotter-than-expected September CPI print pushed December Fed hike odds to roughly 83–89% from ~72% a week earlier, while the US stays funded under the continuing resolution through 11 December, pushing the next shutdown decision past the midterms.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: near-term fiscal certainty for the broader government and short-dated Treasuries as the CR holds through mid-December; cash/money-market holders benefiting from a higher-for-longer rate path. Loses: rate-sensitive equities (Nasdaq −1.88%) and precious metals (gold −1.0%, silver −5.9%), both hit hard as hike odds repriced sharply higher.

desk_stance_html: Wednesday's 641-point rebound shows the market pricing a clean resolution to the KP standoff — NA and Senate ratification plus PPP's about-face removed the two biggest overhangs from Tuesday's session, leaving only today's 11:30am joint sitting as a formality rather than a risk event. The macro base case still argues for a floor: the rupee is flat at 276.95, the SBP holds at 11.5% into its 26 October review, September CPI sits at 10.3%, and the $1.2bn IMF tranche remains pending but not derailed. The swing factor today is imported, not local: a hot US CPI print has pushed December Fed hike odds to ~83–89%, hit gold and silver hard, and left Gulf markets broadly risk-off even with oil firm — none of that is PSX-specific, but a firmer dollar and higher global yields are a headwind for the rupee and import costs over time. Our stance: lean constructive into today's joint sitting, favour the names that already led Wednesday's rally (banks, fertilisers, refineries) on confirmed follow-through, and treat a clean break above 165,629 as confirmation to look toward 167,089 rather than a reason to chase pre-vote. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

linkedin_text:
KSE-100 rebounds 641 points as the KP ratification clears the NA and Senate, while a hot US CPI print sends Wall Street and precious metals sharply lower.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
US stocks sold off Wednesday after September CPI came in hotter than expected at 3.7% y/y (vs 3.6% forecast) with core CPI at 2.6% y/y: the Nasdaq lost 1.88% to 26,692.87, the S&P 500 fell 1.11% to 7,718.94 and the Dow slipped a milder 0.09% to 51,621.48. Treasury yields whipsawed before easing (10Y 5.19%, 2Y 4.82%), while December Fed hike odds jumped to roughly 83-89% from ~72% a day earlier. Gold settled at $4,120.82 (-1.0%) and silver slid 5.9% to $55.70 as the repricing hit precious metals hardest.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 reversed two sessions of selling, climbing 641.07 points (+0.39%) to close at 165,417.51, after the National Assembly and Senate both ratified the federal emergency proclamation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Wednesday (PTI staged a walkout in protest), clearing the way for today's 11:30am joint sitting to formally impose Governor's Rule under Article 234. Buying in ENGROH, LUCK, FFC, BAHL and NBP added 381 points to the index on turnover of roughly 586 million shares worth Rs 20.1 billion. The rupee held flat at 276.95 interbank, the SBP policy rate remains at 11.5% ahead of its 26 October review, September CPI sits at 10.3% y/y, and the $1.2bn IMF tranche still awaits Executive Board sign-off.

GCC
Saudi Arabia's Tadawul All-Share Index fell 1.74% to 10,138.83 on broad-based selling (252 decliners vs 15 advancers), with the Nomu parallel market off 0.90%, even as OPEC+ kept November output quotas unchanged at a combined 31.01 million bpd and Brent held near $105.43 with WTI near $95.17. The UAE's VAT Executive Regulation amendments remain in force, continuing to weigh on SME compliance costs even as the non-oil diversification story stays intact.

GLOBAL
Washington remains funded under the continuing resolution through 11 December, pushing the next shutdown risk past the midterms. The hot CPI print has markets debating whether the Fed delivers a double hike or a 50bp move in December, with odds now near 83-89% for at least one hike.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
- Pakistan: NA/Senate ratify the KP emergency; today's joint sitting formalises Governor's Rule under Article 234 - the federal government and PPP gain, PTI and KP's provincial autonomy lose.
- GCC: OPEC+ holds November output steady + UAE VAT rules stay in force - oil producers and compliant corporates win; UAE SMEs and broader Gulf sentiment (Tadawul -1.74%) lag.
- Global: Hot CPI pushes December hike odds to ~83-89% while the CR funds the government through 11 December - near-term fiscal certainty and cash holders win; rate-sensitive equities and precious metals lose.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 164,060 (deeper support 163,000 if today's vote disappoints), pivot 165,417 (Wednesday's close), resistance 165,629 then 167,089 if the KP vote clears cleanly. Our stance: lean constructive into today's joint sitting, favour the names that already led Wednesday's rally (banks, fertilisers, refineries) on confirmed follow-through, and treat a clean break above 165,629 as confirmation rather than a reason to chase pre-vote. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
